records.name: Niedersachsen
records.summary:
What survives in the record for this Land is framework-level: the July 2026 prison-placement case that drove three Länder to seek a Bundesrat tightening of the federal Self-Determination Act, and a March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the quiet 2023-26 wave of Land prison-placement reforms — which does not name Niedersachsen among the reforming states.

No Lower-Saxon trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding appears in the surviving sources. In a system where criminal law and equality guarantees are federal and prison administration is a Land competence, visitor exposure here follows the national position; the placement debates concern detained people rather than visitors.

records.name: Nordrhein-Westfalen
records.summary:
The surviving record for this Land is framework-level only: the July 2026 prison-placement case that drove three Länder to launch a Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act, and the March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the Land prison-placement reform wave, which does not list this Land among the named reformers.

No North-Rhine-Westphalian trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding survives in the sources; with prison administration a Land competence and criminal-equality law federal, visitor exposure tracks the national position, and the placement reforms bear on detained people.

records.name: Rheinland-Pfalz
records.summary:
Rhineland-Palatinate replaced its prison-execution code with a new § 17, in force 1 March 2026, anchoring inmate placement to the civil-register sex entry — the first reform of the wave that, per a March 2026 constitutional-law survey, made such registry-based placement the majority practice among the Länder. The same essay, written against the July 2026 case in which a prisoner whose legal gender had been changed under the federal Self-Determination Act was sent to a men's prison, argues the registry standard is constitutionally avoidable and some Land versions doubtful, defending inclusive pre-correction placement as constitutional.

These are detained-person rules in a field that is a Land competence; no other Rhineland-Palatine trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding survives in the records, so visitor exposure tracks the national framework.
